extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, Patent Office officials, and courts adjudicating patent matters
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory standards and procedural rules from U.S. patent acts (1836–1842) governing patentability disputes, procedure before the Patent Office, reissues/extensions/disclaimers, evidence/recording, and administrative duties. Useful for practitioners and officials applying historic statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for interfering patents / adverse examiner decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there shall be two interfering patents, or when a patent on application shall have been refused on an adverse decision of a board of examiners on the ground that the patent applied for would interfere with an unexpired patent previously granted, any person interested ... may have remedy by bill in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court, on notice and due proceedings, may adjudge patents void in whole or in part, or inoperative or invalid in any particular part or portion of the United States, according to the parties' interests; may adjudge the applicant entitled to a patent for his invention (or part thereof) according to priority; such adjudication authorizes the Commissioner to issue the patent on filing a copy of the adjudication and otherwise complying with the act. Such judgments affect only the parties and those deriving title from them after rendition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court jurisdiction and injunction power for patent controversies
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under any law granting inventors exclusive rights shall be originally cognizable, as well in equity as at law, by the Circuit Courts of the United States (or District Courts with Circuit Court power).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These courts may, upon a bill in equity filed by any party aggrieved, grant injunctions according to equity principles to prevent violation of inventor rights, on such terms and conditions as they deem reasonable; appeals/writs of error to the Supreme Court lie as provided by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension application and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring an extension beyond the term may apply in writing to the Commissioner, pay $40, and the Commissioner shall publish notice of application in appropriate newspapers; a board (Secretary of State, Commissioner, Solicitor of the Treasury) shall hear evidence for and against extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee must furnish an oath-backed statement of ascertained value and detailed receipts/expenditures; the board, 'having due regard to the public interest,' must be fully satisfied that extension is just and proper because the patentee, without neglect or fault, failed to obtain reasonable remuneration; if so, Commissioner shall renew/extend for seven years from expiration of the first term, enter certificates on record, and extension benefits assignees/grantees to extent of their interests. No extension after patent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Patent Office library resources
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be provided for the use of the Office a library of scientific works and periodical publications, foreign and American, to facilitate duties of the officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriation of $1,500 from the patent fund is provided; acquisition under direction of Committee of the Library of Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification, preservation, and public display of models/specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the duty of the Commissioner to cause models and specimens (compositions, fabrics, manufactures, works of art, patented or unpatented) deposited in the office to be classified, arranged, preserved, and displayed in suitable rooms or galleries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rooms/galleries shall be kept open during suitable hours for public inspection; classification/arrangement should be conducive to beneficial and favorable display and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition of pending actions and applications under repealed prior acts
rubrics_metrics.description: All prior acts/parts of acts on the subject are repealed, but actions and processes in law or equity sued prior to passage may be prosecuted to final judgment and execution as if the act had not been passed, except application of certain sections where applicable; pending patent applications where duty has been paid shall be proceeded with and acted on as though filed after passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves rights and prosecutions begun under earlier statutes, subject to specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-recording patents and deposit of drawings (patents issued prior to Dec 15, 1836)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person in possession of a patent issued prior to Dec 15, 1836 (or recorded assignment) may, without charge, on presentation to the Commissioner, have the same recorded anew in the Patent Office together with descriptions, specifications of claim, and drawings; the Commissioner must transcribe or obtain authenticated copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a drawing was not originally annexed, a delineating drawing, verified by oath as required, may be transmitted and placed on file or copied. Clerks of U.S. judicial courts must transmit authenticated copies they hold when requested by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies as prima facie evidence; recording requirement to be received in evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of such record and drawings, certified by the Commissioner (or chief clerk in his absence), shall be prima facie evidence of particulars of the invention and the patent in any U.S. judicial court in cases where originals would be evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No patent issued prior to Dec 15 shall be received in evidence after June 1 unless recorded anew and a drawing (if separate) verified and deposited; written assignments executed/recorded prior to Dec 15 similarly must be recorded anew to be received as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue/new patent for destroyed or lost original patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent was destroyed (e.g., by the Patent Office fire) or otherwise lost, Commissioner shall, on application by patentee/interest, issue a new patent for the same invention bearing the date of the original patent with a certificate that it was issued pursuant to the act, and enter it of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must deposit a duplicate of the original model, drawings, description, and specification verified by oath as required; such reissued patent and certified copies are admissible as evidence and protect rights to the extent of the original patent and specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement of duplicates of valuable models destroyed
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall procure duplicates of models destroyed by fire that were most valuable/interesting and important to the public or necessary to issue patents, subject to expense limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A temporary board (Commissioner + two Presidential appointees) shall determine which models to obtain and may establish regulations and terms; total expenditure limited (stated amount in act) and duplicates may be obtained at reasonable expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and requirements for multiple reissued patents / deposit before reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is returned for correction and reissue and patentee desires several patents to be issued for distinct parts, he shall pay $30 for each additional patent; no patent made prior to Dec 15 may be corrected/reissued until a duplicate of the original model and drawing verified by oath is deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No addition of an improvement to any prior patent nor new patent for an improvement shall be made to the original inventor/assignee until duplicate model/drawing deposited if Commissioner requires it; compensation for such models/drawings subject to commissioners' judgment under limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent may be issued to assignee; duplicate drawings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patent hereafter to be issued may be made and issued to the assignee(s) of the inventor, the assignment being first entered of record and the specification duly sworn to by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must furnish duplicate drawings whenever the case admits of drawings — one to be deposited in the Office and the other annexed to the patent as part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer procedure for overbroad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patentee has inadvertently claimed more than he was the original inventor of, but some material/substantial part is truly his, he may disclaim such parts not claimed by virtue of the patent, stating extent of his interest; disclaimer must be in writing, attested, recorded on payment of $10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer becomes part of the original specification to the extent of the disclaimant's interest and of those deriving under him after recordation. It does not affect pending actions except insofar as relates to unreasonable neglect or delay in filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/restriction of claims for improvements and reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is made for addition of newly discovered improvement to an existing patent, or when a patent is returned for correction and reissue, the specification of claim shall be subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner shall not add improvement nor grant reissue until applicant enters disclaimer or alters specification in accordance with his decision; dissatisfied applicants have the same remedy and privileges as in original applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of mistaken claims of originality and limits on recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: If by mistake and without wilful default a patentee claimed to be original inventor of a material/substantial part of the thing patented of which he was not the first inventor, the patent shall be deemed good and valid for so much of the invention as is bona fide his own, provided it is material, substantial, and definitely distinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such patentee (or successors) may sue for infringement of the part truly his; however, he shall not recover costs unless he entered a disclaimer at the Patent Office prior to commencement of suit. No benefits if he unreasonably neglected or delayed entering the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of agents to receive/forward models
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner authorized to appoint agents (not exceeding twenty) in principal cities/towns to receive and forward to the Patent Office models, specimens, and manufactures intended to be patented or deposited; transportation chargeable to the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improves access for deposit/filing from different regions of the country; costs borne by patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and compensation for Patent Office clerks and examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of one examining clerk there shall be two examining clerks (specified salaries) and an additional copying clerk; Commissioner may employ temporary clerks as necessary for copying/drafting and for examining/comparing records, with prescribed per-page compensation and reasonable compensation for drawings/comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies salary levels and per-page rates (e.g., seven cents per 100 words) and authorizes flexibility to hire temporary staff as workload requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund to foreign applicants rejected for want of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application of any foreigner for a patent is rejected and withdrawn for want of novelty pursuant to the act, the Commissioner's certificate shall warrant the Treasurer to pay back two thirds of the duty the applicant paid into the treasury on account of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides partial refund to foreign applicants whose applications fail for lack of novelty as certified by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation may substitute for oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an oath is required by the act, if the person is conscientiously scrupulous of taking an oath, affirmation may be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodates religious/ethical objections to oath-taking while preserving evidentiary/substantive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fund accounting and Commissioner reporting duties
rubrics_metrics.description: All moneys paid into the Treasury for patents and fees for copies prior to the act shall be carried to credit of the patent fund; fund appropriated for salaries and other Patent Office expenses, and Commissioner authorized to draw as necessary within limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must lay before Congress annually (in January) a detailed statement of expenditures and payments from the fund and a list of all patents granted (subjects and patentees' residences) and those which became public property, plus other useful information on the state/condition of the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of assistant examiners and temporary clerk compensation (1839)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two assistant examiners shall be appointed with specified salaries; Commissioner authorized to employ temporary clerks for transcribing with compensation not greater than office copy rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts staffing to workload and ties temporary compensation to existing copy rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and distribution of classified alphabetical patent lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner authorized to publish a classified and alphabetical list of all patents granted by the Patent Office prior to publication, retain 100 copies for the Office and deposit 900 copies in the Library of Congress for distribution; appropriation up to $1,000 from the patent fund to defray expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to improve public access and archival distribution of patent information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of foreign patents on U.S. patentability and term limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a U.S. patent by reason of the same having been patented in a foreign country more than six months prior to his U.S. application, provided it has not been introduced into public/common use in the United States prior to the application; every such patent shall be limited to a term of 14 years from the date/publication of such foreign letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows foreign-prior patents to co-exist with U.S. applications under time and public-use limitations and imposes a shortened U.S. term tied to foreign patent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of prior purchasers/users made before inventor's application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or corporation that purchased or constructed a newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend the specific invention so made or purchased without liability to the inventor, and such prior purchase/use does not render a later patent invalid except upon proof of abandonment or that such purchase/sale/prior use was for more than two years prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects good-faith prior users/purchasers; a patent is not automatically invalidated by such prior use unless abandonment or >2 years prior use is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free recording of assignments (repeal of recording fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to pay $3 to the Commissioner for recording any assignment, grant, or conveyance of the whole or any part of the interest under any patent is repealed; such assignments shall be recorded without charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes financial barrier to recording transfers of patent interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of §16 provisions to refusals by Commissioner or Chief Justice; applicant expense responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of the sixteenth section shall extend to all cases where patents are refused for any reason by the Commissioner or Chief Justice upon appeals from the Commissioner's decision, including refusals on account of interference with a prior patent; in cases with no opposing party, a copy of the bill shall be served on the Commissioner and the whole expenses of the proceeding paid by the applicant whether final decision is in his favor or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures equity remedies/priority adjudications apply broadly and places expense burden on applicants when no opposing party appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Chief Justice of D.C. from Patent Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appeal is allowed from the Commissioner's decision to a board of examiners, the party shall have the right instead to appeal to the Chief Justice of the District of Columbia by giving notice to the Commissioner, filing written reasons within time appointed, and paying $25 into the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief Justice will hear and determine such appeals summarily on evidence before the Commissioner, with notice to interested parties; Commissioner must lay original papers and grounds of decision before the judge; Commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath; judge returns papers with certificate which is entered of record and governs further proceedings in the Office; judge's decision does not preclude contesting validity later in judicial courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner power to regulate taking of evidence in contested cases; repeal of board of examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall have power to make regulations respecting the taking of evidence to be used in contested cases before him; the provision for a board of examiners is repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes evidentiary procedure under Commissioner authority and eliminates prior examining board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation to Chief Justice for appellate duties
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be paid annually out of the patent fund to the said Chief Justice, in consideration of the duties imposed, the sum of one hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides modest statutory remuneration for the Chief Justice's summary appellate role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasurer refund authority for mistaken Patent Office fees (1842)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasurer of the United States is authorized to pay back, out of the patent fund, sums of money to any person who shall have paid the same into the Treasury as fees accruing at the Patent Office through mistake and which are not otherwise provided to be paid by existing laws, upon certificate by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows administrative correction/refund of mistaken fee payments from the patent fund when certified by the Commissioner.
